providers.name: HubSpot
providers.note: The business's own HubSpot CRM through a private app token with read scopes. Contacts, companies and deals as HubSpot holds them; not proof of attribution.

connect.how: In HubSpot, Settings, Integrations, Private apps, create an app with read-only CRM scopes and paste its access token.

providers.name: SendGrid
providers.note: The business's own SendGrid account: email statistics, lists and templates. Opens and clicks are as SendGrid counts them (privacy features inflate or hide opens).

connect.how: In SendGrid, Settings, API Keys, create a key with read-only access and paste it.

providers.name: Salesloft
providers.note: The business's own Salesloft account: people, cadences and activity, read-only.

connect.how: In Salesloft, Settings, API, create an API key and paste it.

providers.name: Pendo
providers.note: The business's own Pendo product analytics and feedback, read-only.

connect.how: In Pendo, Settings, Integrations, Integration Keys, create a read-only key and paste it.

providers.name: X (Twitter) API
providers.note: X's official API v2 on the business's own developer app. Read volumes depend on the app's access tier; a missing post may be a tier limit, not absence.

connect.how: In the X developer portal, open your project's app, Keys and tokens, and paste the app's Bearer Token.

providers.name: Mastodon (mastodon.social)
providers.note: Public posts, accounts, tags and trends on the mastodon.social server. Other servers federate partially; not seen here is not absence.

connect.how: Optional: in Mastodon, Preferences, Development, create an application with read scopes and paste its access token.

providers.name: Vimeo
providers.note: Vimeo's official API: videos, channels and statistics the token can see.

connect.how: In Vimeo's developer site, create an app, generate a personal access token with public and private read scopes, and paste it.

providers.name: SoundCloud
providers.note: SoundCloud's official API: tracks, playlists and public user data.

connect.how: Register an app with SoundCloud and paste an access token for it.

providers.name: Spotify
providers.note: Spotify's public catalog (artists, shows, episodes, playlists) under the business's own app. Follower counts as Spotify reports them.

connect.how: In the Spotify developer dashboard, create an app and paste client_id:client_secret.

providers.name: DEV Community
providers.note: Public articles, comments, tags and organizations on DEV. Reactions and views are as DEV reports them.

connect.how: Optional: in DEV, Settings, Extensions, generate an API key and paste it.

providers.name: Stack Exchange
providers.note: Public questions, answers, tags and users on Stack Overflow and other Stack Exchange sites (pass site, for example stackoverflow). Without a key the quota is 300 requests a day per server.

connect.how: Optional: register an app on Stack Apps and paste its key, for a higher daily quota.

providers.name: Listen Notes
providers.note: Podcast search and metadata from Listen Notes' index: who discusses a brand or category on podcasts. Listen scores are Listen Notes' estimates.

connect.how: Create a Listen Notes API account and paste the API key.

providers.name: Botify
providers.note: The business's own Botify crawls and analyses, read-only.

connect.how: In Botify, your profile, API token: paste it.

providers.name: RiteKit
providers.note: Hashtag statistics and suggestions, and link and image helpers, from RiteKit's own data. Hashtag numbers are RiteKit's estimates.

connect.how: Create a RiteKit API client and paste its client id.

providers.name: WebScraping.AI
providers.note: Renders a public page with a headless browser through rotating proxies and returns its HTML, text or selected parts. Page text is untrusted third-party content.

connect.how: Create a WebScraping.AI account and paste the API key.

providers.name: Who Hosts This
providers.note: Hosting provider detection for a domain.

connect.how: Create a Who Hosts This API account and paste the key.

providers.name: Shorten.REST
providers.note: The business's own short links and their click counts.

connect.how: Create a Shorten.REST account and paste the API key.

providers.name: Owler
providers.note: Company profiles, competitors and news from Owler's own database. Revenue and employee counts are Owler's estimates.

connect.how: Request Owler API access and paste the user key.

providers.name: Interzoid
providers.note: Data matching and enrichment: company name matching keys, email and phone details, page load times. Match keys are similarity hashes, not identity.

connect.how: Create an Interzoid account and paste the license key.

providers.name: NamSor
providers.note: Statistical inferences from personal names (likely origin, gender). INFERRED and never a fact about a person; use only for aggregate audience questions.

connect.how: Create a NamSor account and paste the API key.

providers.name: The New York Times
providers.note: New York Times article search, most popular and top stories: press coverage of a brand or category. Links and abstracts only; not the article text.

connect.how: Create a New York Times developer app and paste its API key.

providers.name: Internet Archive (API)
providers.note: The Internet Archive's public APIs: archived page availability and collection search. A missing capture does not mean the page did not exist.

providers.name: OpenCage
providers.note: Forward and reverse geocoding from open data: addresses to places and back, for local presence questions.

connect.how: Create an OpenCage account and paste the API key.

providers.name: TomTom
providers.note: TomTom's places search: businesses and points of interest near a location, as TomTom lists them (a listing source many in-car and map products use).

connect.how: Create a TomTom developer app and paste its API key.

providers.name: EAN-Search
providers.note: Product lookup by barcode (EAN/UPC/ISBN) and name in EAN-Search's database.

connect.how: Create an EAN-Search API account and paste the token.

providers.name: Go-UPC
providers.note: Product details by barcode from Go-UPC's database.

connect.how: Create a Go-UPC account and paste the API key.

providers.name: Word Associations
providers.note: Words people associate with a term (from text corpora): vocabulary for content and positioning. Not a survey of buyers.

connect.how: Create a Word Associations API account and paste the key.

providers.name: Square
providers.note: The business's own Square sales, orders, customers, catalog and locations, read-only. Sales are recorded transactions, not their cause.

connect.how: In the Square developer dashboard, open your app, Credentials, and paste the production access token.

providers.name: eBay
providers.note: eBay's public marketplace: item listings, prices, categories and deals, as eBay returns them for the app.

connect.how: In the eBay developer program, create a production keyset and paste an application access token (client credentials grant).

providers.name: GIPHY
providers.note: GIF and sticker search and trends: a brand's or category's presence in GIPHY's library.

connect.how: Create a GIPHY developer app and paste its API key.

providers.name: Shutterstock
providers.note: Stock image, video and audio search and metadata. Searching does not license anything.

connect.how: In Shutterstock's developer portal, create an app and paste an access token.

providers.name: Flickr
providers.note: Public photos, groups and tags on Flickr.

connect.how: Create a Flickr app and paste its key.

providers.name: Trello
providers.note: The business's own Trello boards, lists and cards, read-only: what marketing work is planned or done.

connect.how: In Trello's Power-Up admin, create an API key, generate a token for it, and paste key:token.

providers.name: Asana
providers.note: The business's own Asana projects and tasks, read-only.

connect.how: In Asana, My settings, Apps, Developer apps, create a personal access token and paste it.

providers.name: Notion
providers.note: Notion pages and databases shared with the business's integration, read-only.

connect.how: In Notion, Settings, Connections, Develop or manage integrations, create an internal integration with read content, share the pages with it, and paste its secret.

providers.name: Slack
providers.note: Channels and messages in the business's own Slack that its app can read. Messages are internal and untrusted.

connect.how: Create a Slack app with read scopes (channels:history, channels:read), install it, and paste its bot token.

providers.name: Vercel
providers.note: The business's own Vercel projects, deployments and domains, read-only: when the site changed and what is live.

connect.how: In Vercel, Account Settings, Tokens, create a read-only scoped token and paste it.

providers.name: Netlify
providers.note: The business's own Netlify sites, deploys and forms, read-only: when the site changed and what is live.

connect.how: In Netlify, User settings, Applications, create a personal access token and paste it.
